$comment: Catalog of coding agents og knows how to wire into Omnigent.
Adding a vendor is a row here, not code. Fields:
id            stable key used in og-install.json state
label         what the picker shows
harness       the Omnigent harness id this agent runs on
binary        what `command -v` looks for during the scan
kind          native      -> Omnigent has a first-class harness
acp-builtin -> Omnigent ships an ACP row for it
acp-user    -> needs an `acp.agents` entry in
~/.omnigent/config.yaml (og writes it)
acp_command   argv for acp-user kinds, e.g. 'cline --acp'
For acp-user kinds `harness` MUST be acp:<slug> where slug is
Omnigent's slugify(label): lowercase, non-alphanumerics -> '-'.
A wrong slug does not error — Omnigent silently falls back to
the FIRST configured acp.agents row, i.e. a different vendor.
roles         which slots it may fill
vendor        model family, used for the cross-vendor review check.
Two agents sharing a vendor cannot review each other.
model.required  true when a dispatch MUST pin a model. Unpinned
workers inherit the ORCHESTRATOR's model id, which
most harnesses cannot resolve.
model.pin_path  where the pin goes in the sub-agent spec. Always
executor.model — executor.config is a free-form dict
and a model placed there is silently ignored.
relay         false when the agent runs without Omnigent's sys_* tool
relay (leaf worker only; cannot orchestrate)
silent_model_failure  true when a bad model id produces an empty
transcript instead of an error
worker        sub-agent name in the bundle. Defaults to coder_<id>; set it explicitly to keep an established name stable across an id change.

multi_account.note: claude-native honours $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, so a second account can run the reviewer independently of your interactive Claude Code login. The in-process claude-sdk harness ignores it.

model.note: Subscription login picks the model. Pinning the ORCHESTRATOR also pins the family its workers route within, which strands non-Claude workers — leave it unset.

agents.label: OpenCode (Zen)

model.note: `opencode models` lists every provider you have added with `opencode auth login` (e.g. deepseek/..., anthropic/...), not just Zen; those bill at the provider's rates. Zen's free `opencode/*-free` lineup rotates, and a paid Zen id on a workspace with no payment method is a FAILED dispatch, not a slower one.

agents.reviewer_warning: Zen's free lineup rotates, so review quality drifts run to run. Not recommended as a reviewer.

quota.note: Zen free tier is enforced server-side with no queryable balance; failures show as 'Rate limit exceeded' in the opencode log (see og audit).

model.note: Picks its own model from the signed-in Google account.

install.note: Ships with the Antigravity editor; `agy` lands in ~/.local/bin.

model.note: Cline ACCEPTS an ACP model switch it cannot serve instead of rejecting it. A wrong id yields 'completed' with an empty transcript and an untouched worktree — no error anywhere. Pin the id `cline auth` actually selected.

quota.note: Only meaningful with a DeepSeek API key in $DEEPSEEK_API_KEY; a Cline-account login has no public balance endpoint yet, so og stats reports unknown.

model.note: Kilo has no bare `auto`; it has an auto-ROUTER family — kilo/kilo-auto/{free,efficient,small,balanced,frontier} — plus kilo/openrouter/auto. `free` keeps it inside the free tier; the others bill at provider rates. Requires `kilo auth` first: an unauthenticated ACP worker fails silently with an empty transcript. An ACP session starts on Kilo's OWN default model (its last-used one, often paid) until the pin is applied; `Add credits to continue, or switch to a free model` means the pin never landed. Put `"model": "kilo/kilo-auto/free"` in ~/.config/kilo/kilo.jsonc so even an unpinned session is free.

agents.label: Kiro (AWS)
agents.kind_note: ACP rather than kiro-native on purpose. Omnigent's headless-worker seam (_derive_terminal_launch_args_from_spec) maps claude/codex/cursor/kimi/agy to their no-prompt flags but has no kiro-native entry, so a native Kiro worker asks for permission on every tool and depends on a tmux permission mirror that fails ('permission prompt was not safely focused before verdict delivery'). Over ACP, Kiro's own --trust-all-tools answers its prompts and permission_mode: bypassPermissions (acp-user) covers what it relays. Revisit once Omnigent maps kiro-native.

model.note: `auto` is Kiro's own default router (1.00x credits, model chosen per task). Over ACP the pin reaches Kiro as the session model (HARNESS_ACP_MODEL); unpinned uses Kiro's default, which is `auto` anyway. Free plan is 50 credits/month from the shared Kiro pool — overflow capacity, not a primary implementer.

quota.note: 50 credits/month on the free plan; no public remaining-credit endpoint found.

model.note: Omnigent always launches `cursor-agent --model <id>`; with no pin the id is the ORCHESTRATOR's (e.g. claude-opus-5[1m]), which cursor-agent rejects (`Cannot use this model`) and exits 1 -- the pane dies before the first prompt and every dispatch reports `Harness stream connection error`. `auto` is Cursor's own router; `cursor-agent models` lists the rest.

install.note: See the Hermes docs for your platform.

model.note: Omnigent's builtin ACP rows own their auth and model selection (OWN_AUTH); a model override is rejected up front rather than silently dropped.

agents.label: Freebuff
agents.kind_note: `blink` (github.com/jmvbambico/bufflink, >= v0.1.2) is an ACP bridge that drives the freebuff TUI in a PTY. Verified 2026-09-20/21 in og-sandbox: five backlog tasks (small to larger, incl. new modules and e2e tests), 3 of 3 first-try since v0.1.2; every commit in scope, gates green. Facts that matter: one blink process = one freebuff launch = one hour billed up front at the chosen model's rate (GLM 5.3 Flash 5/hr by default, up to DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 15/hr) from the free tier's 25 daily Freebucks, so a costlier pin means fewer launches per day, and the process lives as long as the sub-agent SESSION. Omnigent's sys_session_close does NOT end it (observed 2026-09-21): after closing a finished session, `pgrep -x blink` and SIGTERM it - blink exits cleanly within ~5 s and releases freebuff's single-instance lock; verify with `pgrep -fl manicode/freebuff` before the next launch. freebuff writes its transcript only at turn end, so nothing streams while it thinks; all trial turns finished well inside HARNESS_ACP_PROMPT_TIMEOUT_S (300 s), but keep tasks single-purpose. Omnigent's injected system prompt (~5 kB) arrives as a collapsed 'Pasted text' chip, which blink handles; leave inject_system_prompt on. freebuff resolves RELATIVE paths against the cwd omnigent passed (the workspace, not the worktree): dispatch text must use absolute worktree paths and name the gate commands with `cd`. freebuff writes `.freebuff/project-id` into its cwd; gitignore `.freebuff/`. No approval gate: freebuff runs commands unattended - the worktree is the blast radius.

model.note: The model is chosen on freebuff's splash (default GLM 5.3 Flash; the lineup ROTATES - there is a limited-time-trial slot - so `choices` is a convenience list, not a closed set: a free-text id matching a splash display name also works). Pinning one exports BLINK_MODEL=<id> into the worker env; a blink that honours BLINK_MODEL selects it on the splash, older blink accepts the default. A pin naming a model freebuff is not offering fails the dispatch loudly rather than running the default, as does a dispatch into a freebuff hour already running on another model (wait for the hour to end or unset the pin). Vendor follows the model: a deepseek/* pick makes Freebuff same-vendor with Cline for review purposes.

quota.note: freebuff.com exposes no usable quota API (the subscription endpoint returns the SPA); og reports the balance freebuff itself last printed — in chat.db transcripts and runner logs — and unknown when nothing has reported since the daily reset. It never subtracts: freebuff bills per hour at a per-model rate (GLM 5.3 Flash 5/hr, MiMo 2.5 10/hr, Solar Pro 4 10/hr, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 15/hr), so a launch's cost depends on its model and duration. blink fails fast with 'not enough Freebucks' when the pool is empty.

agents.label: Command Code
agents.kind_note: `cmd-acp` (npm, v0.2.0, ~9 commits, last published 2026-08-06, fork of soycanopa/cmd-acp) bridges ACP to `cmd -p`, spawning one `cmd -p` process per prompt. It exposes model, reasoning effort and permission mode ONLY through the ACP method session/set_config_option, which Omnigent never sends (the acp_command docstring in og_install.py traces the wire). Its session config therefore starts EMPTY: no --model and, critically, no --yolo. Headless runs still go through Command Code's permission engine, so without --yolo the worker returns end_turn having changed nothing — the 'completed with no output' signature. The bridge does honour the env var CMD_BIN to choose the binary it spawns (dist/index.js, resolveCmdBinary), and passes the parent env through to it. That is why og points CMD_BIN at a generated shim instead of patching or forking the bridge. --tools-all is needed because headless runs withhold some tools; --skip-onboarding is needed because Command Code otherwise runs a taste-onboarding step on first launch. Setting permissions.defaultMode = yolo in ~/.commandcode/settings.json is the alternative to the shim, but it applies globally to the user's interactive cmd too and cannot carry --tools-all. The shim keeps it per-worker. Unlike freebuff/blink there is no long-lived process to reap: each prompt is one `cmd -p` that exits.

model.note: (a) ids are provider-prefixed for open-weight models (moonshotai/…, deepseek/…, z-ai/…) but BARE for Anthropic and OpenAI (claude-sonnet-5, gpt-5.5); (b) vendor MUST follow the pinned model, exactly as the freebuff row says — pinning deepseek/* makes this same-vendor with Cline, z-ai/* same-vendor with Freebuff, meta/muse-spark-* same-vendor with OpenCode's pin, and claude-*/gpt-* same-vendor with the orchestrator and reviewer; the default moonshotai pin is chosen because no other roster member uses that vendor; (c) an unpinned run is a SUCCESSFUL cmd invocation on cmd's own default model, which is why silent_model_failure is true.

quota.note: Command Code enforces a rolling 5-hour AND a rolling weekly credit window, both rolling from first use, on top of the monthly credit pool (Go $1/$10, GOAT $10/$70, Pro $20/$80, Max 10x $100/$150, Max 20x $200/$300; Pro's windows are $16 per 5h and $40 per week). No queryable quota API. Exhaustion prints `You've reached your 5-hour usage limit. Resets in 2h 41m` — match that string to mark the worker dry and take --until from it.

$prompt_delivery.argv: Prompt is appended to the CLI argv at startup. Subject to the tmux command-string ceiling (PROMPT_CEILING).
$prompt_delivery.per_turn: Prompt is composed and sent per turn over the harness's own transport. No command-line ceiling.
$prompt_delivery.first_user: Prompt is prepended to the first user message.
$prompt_delivery.none: The harness NEVER receives the spec prompt. A worker on this harness only ever sees the dispatch text, so operating rules must be inlined into args.input by the orchestrator. Cannot be an orchestrator.
$prompt_delivery.unknown: Not declared by Omnigent (user-configured ACP). Assume the prompt may not arrive; inline critical rules in the dispatch.

$quota.description: Optional per-agent `quota` blocks drive `og stats` (see docs/STATS.md). `probe` is the stats-layer probe name; it is null when the limit is known but exposes no queryable API, so `og stats` reports it as unknown rather than guessing. `daily` is the pool size consumed by the launch-budget probe (freebuff); that probe reports the balance freebuff itself last printed and never subtracts a per-launch cost.
